title: Snoozer Quinn's life and electric guitar
summary: He gives Quinn's origins, appearance and character, his guitar playing at Werlein's, and his liking for an electric pickup.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Where did he come from? Do you remember anything about his life at all, early life? Did he ever say anything?

Born in Buggaloosa and his family is still there. His brother visited me not so long ago, several years ago, to get some records from me that Snoozer had made. He was a man of his family. And, you know, you never saw him, huh?
His head was deformed in a peculiar way. It was sort of bent.
It may have been from Fawcett's when he was born. Yeah. But he was such an awful nice man, too. Such an awful nice fellow. There wasn't a mean thing in him. He never said a mean word about anybody.
He was just a marvelous person. Most of the best musicians I found in that way. Yeah. The very best.

And this guy played guitar the whole time he was out of bed. He got up in the morning and picked up that doggone guitar, and I don't think he ever let it go until he carried it around with him, or either he always... When I was working at Whirline's, he'd come in, and it wouldn't be two seconds before the whole store was around Snoozer Quinn. He'd pick up one of the guitars, and he'd say, let me see that guitar over there, and he'd start playing on it. Did he ever play an electric guitar?
I guess they didn't have them early in those days.

You can believe it or not, those poor guitar players are so frustrated by the instrument not being heard that Snoozer, even Snoozer, like an electric guitar. Yes, sir, he had a rig up on those records that I made that long ago.

And I had a terrible time to keep him from using it, and he used it on three or four sides. Oh, I don't remember that. Yeah. He used that thing on three or four sides. I couldn't keep him away from it.
It is weak tone. You'll have to admit it.

Yeah, they're frustrated. You know, they had all these trombones blowing their heads off in a flock of cornets in the back, like when he was with Whiteman, you know. And there his poor little guitar there, nobody could hear it. What are you going to do with it? You know, no. You've got to put a microphone right in front of it. Well, the electric guitar takes the place of that. And of course, we all think it's a horrible sound, and I'll never get over thinking how horrible that sound is, and I'll never like them. But you can't blame people. Even Bill Clevenger wants to get a rig, has been wanting to get a rig for his mandolin for years, you know, an electrical pickup. And everybody's been talking him out of it, you know. It's a week, too.
Yeah, sure, it's the same conditioning up with guitar. But that may have been one of the reasons that Snoozer left Whiteman, or maybe Whiteman felt like he couldn't be heard.
